Hi Hannah/Kimberly,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the latency profiles look promising for our triage workflows. We're kicking off an internal discussion about whether to extend the pilot window and also explore pricing structures that tie discounts to measurable outcomes. Two quick asks: 

1) Would Redwood consider an outcome-based rebate tied to two milestone metrics (ingest accuracy > 88% and average inference latency < 220ms for the test set)?
2) If yes, could you draft a short milestone split (e.g., 30% rebate if both met, 15% if one met) and show how that maps to the pilot invoice?

We need this to present to procurement by next Tuesday. I attached an internal SOW outline for reference.

Thanks,
Ari Torres
Director, AI Platforms — Lumina Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline and outcome-based rebate idea

Hi Ari — great to hear the demo landed well. Appreciate the clarity on procurement timing. We can absolutely propose an outcome-linked structure for a timeboxed pilot. Below are two clean options for Lumina to review; I copied Priyom for technical validation and Kimberly for commercial sign-off.

Option A — Milepost Rebate (preferred)
- Pilot length: 8 weeks (no changes to infra access)
- List invoice: $24,000 (flat pilot fee covering reserved throughput + support)
- Mileposts (measured on canonical test set at week 6 + week 8):
  * M1: Ingest accuracy >= 88% (pass/fail)
  * M2: Average inference latency <= 220ms (p95 target)
- Rebate: 30% of pilot fee if both M1+M2 met; 15% if exactly one met; 0% if none met
- Operational notes: Redwood will provide a short verification script and runbook; results will be jointly validated and captured in a 1‑page attestation.

Option B — Time extension + modest credit
- Extend pilot by 2 weeks; invoice unchanged but add a $6k credit reserve if both metrics met at extension close
- Lower upside (max 25% effective rebate) but simpler for procurement to treat as credit vs refund

Recommendation: Option A keeps incentives aligned and simplifies the accounting (single rebate event after validation). If legal needs an escrow-style clause, we can add a conditional payment term.

Next steps:
- Kim: can you confirm commercial willingness to accept the 30%/15% split (we can cap total rebate at $7,200)?
- Priyom: can you confirm the validation run takes ~2 hours and whether there are any data/labeling caveats?
- Ari: once you confirm the structure I will send a one-page amendment + updated SOW and DocuSign link.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform

Attachments: Pilot_Milestones.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Pilot timeline and outcome-based rebate idea — internal commercial/ops notes

Kim, Priyom — forwarding Ari's ask and my draft above. High-level thoughts: 

- Commercial tolerance: I'd like to cap the rebate to protect margin. Suggest cap = $7,200 (30% of $24k). Also propose a clause that the rebate is applied as a credit against the final invoice rather than a cash refund — less finance friction.
- Legal: We should avoid long-term SLA promises for pilot. Keep the validation as a short attestation (joint signature) rather than a unilateral Redwood measurement.
- Ops: Priyom, confirm the verification script and what counts as the canonical test set. If the customer needs us to run on more than one dataset, we should limit to two runs to avoid open-ended work.

Suggested negotiation script for Ari: "We can do the 30%/15% milepost rebate with a $7.2k cap, applied as a credit on the final pilot invoice. Redwood and Lumina will co-sign a one‑page attestation that validates the test run and results."

If you approve, I'll put this in a 1-page amendment and send to Ari with a DocuSign link.

— H
